cells.tense: A chapter here is genuinely finished, and with the pen in hand you can feel that without needing to seal it shut.
cells.act: meet what is arriving as it arrives
cells.ask: Let whatever reaches you first today arrive whole — a voice, a message, the cold at the window — before you sort it into meaning or place.
cells.core:
A cycle closes and you can feel it close without needing it to keep talking. Nothing else is required: something is done, you are still here, and the next part is not yours to haul in ahead of time. Ending a thing and staying open are not opposites.

Where it bends is the small addendum you write underneath — the almost, the also, the I-should-still. Meet what comes without adding it. Someone speaks and you take the words as the first time they have been said, not the ninth in a line. Finished work sits out in the open, and you let it sit. What closes well is what opens next.
cells.sheetLine: Something is done, and you are still here in the light.
cells.verb: closing a cycle so the next one has a door
cells.place: at the doorway where what couldn't hold just gave way

cells.tense: You will have shut the book before the last page is written, already living in the after of a story still going.
cells.act: receive the thing that is coming instead of bracing for it
cells.ask: When you catch yourself marking something complete, hold one breath back before the name lands and take what is actually present instead.
cells.core:
You are marking things done ahead of schedule. Something begins and part of you is already past it — saying the goodbyes, filing the lessons, naming the shape before it has one. The instinct for closing arrives early, and what is still alive gets treated as already over.

What actually works is receiving the thing itself, not the ending you have already sketched. When you see the whole arc in a flash, stay with the moment only. Not the lesson, not the meaning. The meeting. A cycle takes its own length; your work is to be at the door when it genuinely shuts, not to shut it on time.

cells.tense: A search finished somewhere back and you are still at its edge, asking it for one more page.
cells.act: take the turning as it comes
cells.ask: Take a question you have carried past its usefulness and set it down finished rather than solved — then look at the plain afternoon that is left.
cells.core:
You keep a lot open. Closing something has felt like losing what sits behind it, so you stand half in a dozen entryways rather than step fully through one. What is done does not need you stationed at its edge. It has already gone through.

The turn has already happened. A search, a maybe, a question asked past its answer: set it down as finished and see the room you are actually in. What looked like a threshold was the room. More is waiting than you are letting reach you, and letting something be done is how the next thing gets to count.
cells.sheetLine: You keep asking an entryway that has already closed.

cells.tense: Cycles have been closing in your life without your marking them, and you file them as things that happened to you rather than as your own moves.
cells.act: let go of the thing you are gripping
cells.ask: Set down a worry, a plan, a role you have carried from habit — on purpose, once — and let your hands rest without it for an afternoon.
cells.core:
Things finish around you and you do not file them as finished. A job, a friendship, a season has already turned, and you treat it as the current conditions — something happening to you, not something you walked through. Those turns were yours. You simply have not had a hand on the pen.

Release what you grip without knowing you grip it. Not by losing it, not by having it pulled away — on purpose, once. What has been quietly ending gets to end, and what arrives next can arrive at a door you know you opened. Your life has been moving; seeing that comes back first, and then the hand on the pen.
cells.sheetLine: Your life keeps turning and you haven't signed for any of it.
